sources.title: January 2019 interview: 1984 birth, Mbororo rights, AFPAT’s 1999 foundation and 2005 legal status
sources.findings: Read the UNESCO Courier interview published 15 January 2019, later updated 27 April 2023. Its biographical paragraph explicitly gives 1984 in Chad, and the interview separates AFPAT creation in 1999 from legal status in 2005. No January 1 birthday is inferred from year-only data. It discusses rights, education, health, justice, women’s participation and environmental knowledge. Her descriptions of gains and deficiencies are interview testimony, not a fresh 2026 legal audit. The old reference to Idriss Déby as current president is historical; neither this office nor other 2019 conditions are carried forward as current.

sources.title: 2015 interview: N’Djamena birth, community advocacy and association registration
sources.findings: Read the 2015 Pollution atmosphérique interview’s introduction and formation-history answer. It supports N’Djamena birthplace, Mbororo/Fulani identity, her mother’s support for schooling, 1999 creation and 2005 operating permission. Sources elsewhere describe activism beginning at 12, association creation at 15 or 16, and one indexed later interview collection gives 2006 recognition; do not force these into one certain age/date sequence. The timeline attributes 2005 to the two directly read interviews, not to an inspected registration certificate. Introductory generalisations about girls’ marriage or literacy are not applied to every Mbororo woman or to all Indigenous peoples.

sources.title: Hindou Ibrahim biography: community mapping, international advocacy and 2018 indigenous fellowship
sources.findings: Read the UN Office for Partnerships profile, including the fuller biography. It supports AFPAT founding/leadership, community-based mapping, work across climate/biodiversity/desertification discussions and senior Indigenous fellowship at Conservation International since 2018. The page alternates present and past tense for international climate-forum co-chairmanship; no unrefreshed current claim for that office is adopted. Its National Geographic Explorer recognition is not a geography degree or university appointment. The 2018 fellowship is an institutional role; no unverified degree or exact appointment month is invented.

sources.title: 22 April 2016 signing-ceremony report: Ibrahim speaks as a civil-society representative in New York
sources.findings: Read the relevant opening/location and Ibrahim intervention passages of IISD Earth Negotiations Bulletin’s 22 April 2016 report. It confirms actual speech at UN Headquarters, New York, as a civil-society representative, with adaptation-finance and climate-impact concerns. The Paris name belongs to the agreement, not the location of this signing event. She was not thereby Chad’s state signatory, a head of state, or sole author of the treaty. A preparatory UN press notice alone would be prospective; this contemporaneous report supplies the completed-event evidence. No complete recording or all national speeches were reviewed.

sources.title: 9 May 2019 appointments: six new SDG advocates including Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim
sources.findings: Read the concise IISD SDG Knowledge Hub report: 9 May 2019, six new advocates including Ibrahim, taking the group to 17. The public text distinguishes the number newly appointed from the full group. SDG advocacy is not an administrative headship of the UN Secretariat or national executive office. The named co-chairs and other members in this 2019 article are historical; their present positions are not inferred. UN primary announcement/briefing bodies were inaccessible, while their indexed dates and appointment snippets corroborate the readable report.

sources.publisher: UCLA Institute of the Environment and Sustainability
sources.title: 8 November 2019 report on the 7 November Pritzker Emerging Environmental Genius Award
sources.findings: Read UCLA’s 8 November 2019 report. It explicitly places the award ceremony on 7 November at Hershey Hall, gives US$100000 and identifies the Pritzker Emerging Environmental Genius Award. It is not the architecture prize, and the 8 November publication date is not the ceremony date. Mapping methods are described as gathering resource knowledge from multiple local groups; reports of reduced tension are project accounts, not an independent impact experiment. Its 90 percent Lake Chad decline since 1980 differs from later sources’ 1960s baseline and was omitted. Its prospective 2020 Glasgow event is not proof of a conference subsequently occurring on that schedule.

sources.title: Indexed laureate profile: 2021 award and participatory resource-mapping project
sources.findings: Read the indexed Rolex laureate profile and indexed five-winners announcement. They identify a 2021 award for combining Indigenous knowledge with natural-resource mapping and climate adaptation. The profile says published November 2022, while the indexed jury account describes selection in November 2020; neither replaces the 2021 award year. Opening these legacy Rolex pages redirected to current general watch/newsroom pages, so no claim is made to have read their recovered full bodies. No grant amount, exact announcement day or independently proven conflict-prevention outcome is asserted.

sources.publisher: United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues
sources.title: E/2024/43–E/C.19/2024/8: election of the chair at the first meeting on 15 April 2024
sources.findings: Read the relevant organisation-of-session and bureau-election paragraphs of final UN report E/2024/43–E/C.19/2024/8. Paragraph 164 dates the first meeting to 15 April 2024 and paragraph 167 identifies Ibrahim as elected chair, with Aluki Kotierk among the vice-chairs. This establishes the twenty-third-session chairmanship, not a permanent office or an unlimited mandate. No claim to have read all recommendations or all pages of the report is made.

sources.title: July 2026 statement by chair Aluki Kotierk on the twenty-fifth Forum session
sources.findings: Read the heading and introductory report-presentation passage of the ECOSOC statement dated 21–22 July 2026. It identifies chair Aluki Kotierk and the twenty-fifth Forum session held 20 April–1 May 2026. This prevents carrying Ibrahim’s 2024 chair title forward as the current 2026 chair. It does not by itself establish Ibrahim’s exact last day in office, every intervening chair election, or whether she retained another Forum membership; no such dates or claims are invented.

sources.publisher: Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation
sources.title: 17 October 2026 release: 16 October Planetary Health Awards and Ibrahim’s Awareness award
sources.findings: Read the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation’s 17 October 2026 release: ceremony on Friday 16 October, named laureates and acceptance of awards. Ibrahim’s category is Awareness for Indigenous rights and traditional ecological knowledge, distinct from David Obura’s Science award and CorPower Ocean’s Innovation and Solutions award. No coral-reef research, wave-energy invention, projected electricity output or IPBES chairmanship is attributed to her. The report documents a completed award reception, not simply nomination or a future invitation; no photo pixels or ceremony video were reviewed.

sources.title: 9 November 2026 article by AFPAT president Ibrahim on water, land rights and local climate finance
sources.findings: Read the 9 November 2026 bylined SDG Action article, author role, and sections on land rights, participatory mapping, cross-border cooperation and direct local finance. It identifies her as AFPAT president and supplies recent authorship evidence, not independent proof of an in-person event. The policy prescriptions and claims about project effects remain attributed. No independent audit of all project outcomes, climate-finance percentages or Lake Chad surface-area estimates was performed; the 90-percent statistic and population counts were not imported. Its age-12 activism shorthand does not change the 1999 association date or prove foundation at age 12.

sources.title: 23 September 2026 climate and just-transition event: Ibrahim’s attributed intervention
sources.findings: Read the UN transcript page heading dated 23 September 2026 and the moderator introduction and Ibrahim intervention around 4:54:25. It names her as an SDG Advocate and AFPAT president and records discussion of knowledge, decision-making power, resources and community consent. It is a transcript preview with apparent transcription errors, not a verified verbatim edition; no audio/video was reviewed. The dossier paraphrases broad themes rather than reproducing uncertain wording or transferring other speakers’ statistics and statements to her. This supports recent public activity separately from the November byline.

portraitReview.credit: Fatakaya; own work, transferred from French Wikipedia by JinSakai
portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons description, date, author, own-work declaration, licence, EXIF dates and upload history. The image is dated 24 September 2015, with 13:53 metadata; JinSakai transferred it from French Wikipedia on 13 November 2018. Fatakaya is the credited creator, not the transfer uploader. The original is listed as 1126×1139 and 323 KB, while the absent older cache record has 182961 bytes; that record is not proof of downloaded original bytes. CC BY-SA 4.0 requires credit, licence link, indication of modifications and compatible share-alike treatment of adaptations. Original download on 18 November returned curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000, and the exact referenced cache is missing. Identity, original colour, crop and actual sharpness/resolution remain visually unreviewed.
